history.dynasty: Local chiefs (rural kings, per temple lore)
history.summary: CSV TOWN FLAG: actual town is Uthukuli, about 15 km from Tiruppur (not Tiruppur itself). Legend: the saint Agastiyar came to meditate on Kathithamalai hill but found no water; Murugan thrust his vel into the sand, releasing a spring - hence 'Uthukuli'. Local tradition holds the temple was built about 200 years ago by rural kings and was rebuilt with donor support in recent years (one source says 'five years before' its undated write-up; exact dates unverified). The deity is Vetri Velayudha Swami. Its signature feature is the temple car (ther), pulled up the hill slopes - described as unique to this hill. Daily attendance is small (one source cites 200+ visitors a day).

name: Uthukuli Murugan Temple
town_description: Uthukuli is a small town in Tiruppur district, Tamil Nadu, about 15 km from Tiruppur city on the route towards Avinashi; the temple stands on Kathithamalai hill just outside it.

travel.road: Uthukuli is ~15 km from Tiruppur city by road on the Tiruppur-Avinashi route
